messages.subject: Generating NicheMapR/microclim daily values
parts:
Hi All,

I am a graduate student at Penn State University, and I am currently investigating plasticity in metabolic rate and the impact of climate warming on terrestrial salamanders. In particular I am interested in the impact of warming on length and intensity of summer heat.

I am now trying to predict summer maintenance energy costs across the range (northeastern USA) of my species. I have created a 30 year climate normal for each day of the year using PRISM climate data, but ideally I would like to have surface temperatures for forested conditions. I have been exploring both microclim and NicheMapR.

From what I can tell, the best way to get 365 days of climate data is using the micro_global function; however, I am looking for climate data across multiple areas instead of a specific location as requested in the function arguments. I also can't tell which data is coming from a climate normal or from a weather station in the package.

I would be very grateful if you could provide some guidance on how to generate the following using either microclim or NicheMapR (if it is possible).

1) a daily microclimate normal raster for a defined area (e.g. Northeast)
2) projecting the daily climate normals into the future

Thank you for your time,

David Muñoz

messages.author: 9c7ab3c81d833137
messages.subject: Re: Generating NicheMapR/microclim daily values
parts:
Hi David,

I think Mike will reply at some point but here's what I would do:

1. Gather cell centroids (x,y coords) for each point across your study area at your desired resolution. You could do with raster:rasterToPoints.
2. Loop NicheMapR::micro_global across all these points. Set the argument timeinterval=365 to generate estimates for every day of the year. 

This will generate microclim estimates from the original CRU TS data, unless you create your own custom climate dataset. Be warned - the returned list from looping across a large spatial extent will get very large, very quickly, especially if you want to run it at a daily resolution.

To predict into the future you'd likely have to create your own climate stack to feed into the micro_clim model. But remember that micro_global requires inputs at a reference height (but I think this can be changed with an argument...I forget which one). 

Hope that helps.

messages.author: 9c7ab3c81d833137
messages.subject: Re: Generating NicheMapR/microclim daily values
parts: I forgot to add; once you've generated your microclim estimates you can extract what values you'd like from micro$environ. For example, you could take the max temperature for day, cbind that values with your original list of xy coordinates and then reproject this as a raster using raster::rasterfromxyz.

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Generating NicheMapR/microclim daily values
parts:
Hi David,

Simon's suggestions are spot on re using micro_global. If you haven't already, it might be worth going through the vignettes in the package that describe the microclimate model and provide examples.

For the US I've included a function, 'micro_usa', which connects to the daily gridMET meteorological grids. That would allow you to use historical daily data to run the model. You can either connect via opendap or download the gridMET data locally from here http://www.climatologylab.org/gridmet.html and point the function to the location via the argument 'spatial'.

I'm also producing a gridded microclimate data set for the USA based on the gridMET data, similar to one I've just made for Australia. The Australian one is here: https://knb.ecoinformatics.org/#view/doi:10.5063/F1Q23XFS and there's a manuscript in review at the moment describing it. The Australian and US data sets are every ~60 km (i.e. around 2,300 point estimates across the USA), but hourly, going back to 1979 in the case of the US data set. I haven't made future projections for these.

There's also Levy et al.'s USA microclimate data set, which can be found here https://knb.ecoinformatics.org/#view/doi:10.5063/F1Z899CZ,  but I haven't used it myself as yet and can't advise you much more about it.

All the best,
Mike
